notes: Verdicts must be resolved against the installed ~/.claude/model-profiles.md, never from memory. Assertions deliberately contain NO model strings: the previous version pinned them and went stale the moment tier_to_model changed, which is the same defect the skill exists to prevent. Assert the placement, the tier, the effort, and the LOOKUP PATH (tier_to_model[x] for a session, delegation_aliases[x] for a subagent); whether the resolved value is current is the job of meta.staleness_rule and the SessionStart hook. Each case names the failure mode it guards. Run with-skill vs baseline; grade each assertion with quoted evidence.

evals.name: delegation-emits-alias-never-null
evals.guards: Observed defect: four subagents silently inherited the escalation tier because the Agent call's `model` was left null on prompts that already contained the method.
evals.prompt: I'm running this session on Fable. I want a subagent to apply the already-specified rename across the 12 call sites and run the test suite. What should I give it?
assertions: Answers `Where: delegate` first — the unit has a stateable contract and a named verification command
Emits execution tier at effort high
Emits the target as an Agent-tool `model` ALIAS resolved from delegation_aliases[execution], not a model string from tier_to_model
States that leaving `model` null makes the subagent inherit the caller's model, i.e. this unit would run on the escalation tier
Does not recommend keeping the work in the session

evals.name: recon-delegation-and-its-hard-limits
evals.guards: The cheapest tier is the one most often skipped; and it is the only current model whose context window and effort handling differ.
evals.prompt: Find every place the retry/backoff policy is configured in this service and summarize what each one sets.
assertions: Answers `Where: delegate` with recon tier at effort low
Resolves the target from delegation_aliases[recon]
Surfaces at least one recon-profile delta that actually breaks a delegation — the 200K context window, or that `effort` errors on that model
Does not route a pure lookup to a judgment tier

evals.name: session-deliberation-no-over-escalation
evals.guards: Over-routing: treating 'hard' as a synonym for the escalation tier.
evals.prompt: Design a caching layer for these DB calls — the invalidation is tricky. Which model?
assertions: Answers `Where: this session` — the work is the judgment
Emits deliberation tier at xhigh (or high, with a stated reason)
Resolves the target from tier_to_model[deliberation]
Does NOT pick the escalation tier, and says why: no escalate_when signal has fired and 'hard' is not one
Names a Watch signal that would justify escalating later

evals.name: consequence-override-beats-task-shape
evals.guards: Reversibility, not size, sets the floor. A one-line change to persistent state is not recon work.
evals.prompt: Tiny change: flip the default on this column in the production migration so new rows get the new value. One line. Which model?
assertions: Applies routing_rubric.consequence_override and floors the tier at deliberation despite the task looking like trivial execution
Names the reason as reversibility/persistent state, not difficulty
Does not route it to recon or execution on the grounds that the diff is one line

evals.name: phased-task-routed-per-phase
evals.guards: Averaging a mixed task into one verdict.
evals.prompt: Plan, implement, and review a new billing module. What model per phase?
assertions: Emits one line per phase rather than a single averaged verdict
Each line carries a placement (session vs delegate) as well as a tier and effort
Plan and review resolve to the deliberation tier; implement resolves to the execution tier
The implement phase is marked delegable and carries an alias, not a model string

evals.name: mid-run-handoff-not-in-place-escalation
evals.guards: The flagship case: a stuck run whose framing is wrong. Raising the tier inside that session keeps the bad framing; a fresh session re-derives it.
evals.prompt: I've been on this defect for hours. Two different fixes both failed the same way, and I've re-explained the same constraint to you twice. Should I switch to a stronger model?
assertions: Names the fired execution_signals.escalate_when items — the defect surviving two independent fix attempts, and the constraint restated twice
Answers `Where: fresh session`, NOT raising the tier inside the current session
Cites session_lifecycle.hand_off — a long session defends its own earlier conclusions
Requires session_lifecycle.externalize first and names the file the durable state goes to
Points at tailor-to-fable to write the handoff brief

evals.name: de-escalation-the-under-used-direction
evals.guards: Staying on a premium tier after the judgment is finished; de_escalate_when never fires because nobody checks it.
evals.prompt: Good — that diagnosis is right, the bug is the missing guard in the reducer. The fix is the same three-line pattern in each of the 9 reducers, and `pnpm test` covers it. Keep going?
assertions: Fires execution_signals.de_escalate_when — the unknown resolved, and the remainder repeats an established pattern with a verification command
Drops the tier rather than continuing at the current one
Also flips the placement to delegate, and emits the alias from delegation_aliases
Does not treat the fact that the session is already on a higher tier as a reason to stay there

evals.name: graceful-staleness-flags-one-half-only
evals.guards: A blanket STALE flag on a profile whose API facts are current is noise, and noise gets ignored.
evals.prompt: Which model for reviewing this PR? (assume the deliberation profile's prompting_verified is 90 days old and unreachable, but its api_verified is current)
assertions: Still emits the durable verdict: deliberation tier with an effort
Flags prompting_verified as stale and does NOT flag api_verified or the tier_to_model string
Withholds or hedges the posture/nuance line rather than asserting a nuance it cannot verify
Does NOT invent or guess a model string
